Draw the W of Cassiopeia on the land in light. Then its five bright stars burst out of the ground one by one, dimmest first, each crater as wide as its star is bright, each leaving a glowing star core standing in it while the star itself climbs into the sky and hangs there. The brightest, Schedar, comes last, the W shines in the sky above its twin on the land, and veins of starlight run along the W between the craters. Power widens it all; Damage is what the blasts do (infinity erases what stands in a crater).
